name: DC motor with fan blade (130 size)

provenance.notes: The kit ships one 'Motor & Fan': a metal-can motor of the common 130 size (SunFounder's Motor page shows a 130-style can with a white end cap and two solder lugs) with two wire leads, one red and one black, plus a separate three-blade plastic fan blade (white blades on a yellow hub) for the shaft. SunFounder gives no motor datasheet. The values below are from the 130-size toy/hobby motor sheet (Adafruit product 711 text, read from the components101.com copy), the closest published datasheet for a 130 motor with breadboard-friendly wires; they are not confirmed for the kit's unbranded unit. Sheet values: rated 6.0 VDC, working range 4.5 to 9 VDC (stated in its description), no-load current 70 mA max, no-load speed 9100 +/-1800 rpm, loaded current 250 mA max and loaded speed 4500 +/-1500 rpm at the 10 g*cm rated load, starting torque 20 g*cm, starting voltage 2.0, stall current 500 mA max (the sheet does not say at which voltage), body 27.5 x 20 x 15 mm, shaft 8 mm long and 2 mm dia, weight 17.5 g. The datasheet gives NO terminal resistance or inductance, so none is recorded: measure the kit's motor with a multimeter. The kit runs it at 5 V from the power module through an L293D (SunFounder's Motor page), which is inside the sheet's 4.5 to 9 V range but below the 6 V rating, so speed will be lower than the no-load figure. Ratings of 130-size motors differ widely between models, so do not reuse these numbers for a different 130 motor. Connectors: in SunFounder's component photo each lead ends in a black Dupont-style housing with a thin metal male pin sticking out, so both pins are 'male-pin'. In real use those pins plug straight into breadboard holes; the app's off-board model joins an off-board pin to a hole through a lead, so a male-female Dupont lead stands in for that direct plug until a pre-wired-lead footprint exists. Direction of rotation for a given polarity is not specified by any source read; the leads are not polarised electrically. The fan blade (SunFounder's component photo, no dimensions given anywhere) spins with the shaft; its diameter is unknown and is not modelled here.
